title: Finca San Juan residents protest a planned eviction near Demasa
organizer: Residents of Finca San Juan; no formal organization named in the report
participants_original: No attendee count reported. The article says 250 families could be affected by eviction; this is not a protest-participant count.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved. The contemporaneous report describes residents blocking streets but supplies no simultaneous participant total. Its 250-family figure describes affected households, not attendance.

start_date.summary: Telediario dates the residents' protest to the morning of Friday, Jan. 20, 2023.

location.summary: The report places the gathering near Demasa in Pavas, San José.

organizer.summary: The report identifies residents of Finca San Juan; it names no formal organization.

demands.summary: Residents asked the Municipality of San José to halt the planned Jan. 25 eviction and respect a precautionary measure; coded provisionally as a land/housing issue.

participants_original.summary: No crowd size is given. The 250-family figure refers to households at risk, not demonstrators.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numerical attendance or explicit evidence of at least 50 simultaneous participants.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or time is reported.

state_response.summary: The article reports police presence and regulated traffic but does not describe an event-specific response in any coded state-response dimension; values remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not establish whether protesters used violence; silence is not coded as no.

state_target.summary: Residents directed their request to the Municipality of San José over the scheduled eviction and precautionary measure.

notes: The request concerns a municipal eviction. Police presence and periodic vehicle passage are reported; neither establishes a response category. Keep distinct from the UCR-indexed Jan. 21 municipal-office lead until its underlying record and relationship are clarified.
open_questions: Verify at least 50 simultaneous participants without counting affected households.
Resolve whether the UCR-indexed Jan. 21 municipal-office action is a distinct gathering or the same episode recorded differently.
Keep the physical end date/time and state-response dimensions unknown unless event-specific evidence is found.

title: March for justice for Keylor Gamboa from Parque Central to the Supreme Court
location: Parque Central to the entrance of the Supreme Court, San José
organizer: Michelle Madrigal, Keylor Gamboa's girlfriend, with family and friends
participants_original: Both CR Hoy and La Teja describe 'decenas de personas'; neither gives a numerical total.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved. Two reports use the qualitative description 'decenas' without defining a count or establishing at least 50 simultaneous participants; no numeric bounds are inferred.

start_date.summary: La Teja reports the walk began on Friday, Jan. 20, 2023.

start_time.summary: La Teja reports an actual 9:30 a.m. start at Parque Central; CR Hoy's 9:00 a.m. time is a quoted invitation, not the observed start.

end_date.summary: La Teja says the route ended at the Supreme Court entrance on the same Friday; no end time is provided.

location.summary: Both outlets report a route from Parque Central to San José courts; La Teja identifies the endpoint as the Supreme Court entrance.

organizer.summary: CR Hoy names Michelle Madrigal, family, and friends; La Teja identifies Madrigal as leading the activity.

demands.summary: The march sought justice for Keylor Gamboa and his family; CR Hoy also records a call for stricter laws. The state target is the justice process/lawmakers, coded provisionally as political behavior/process.

participants_original.summary: Both articles use 'decenas de personas' and give no numeric crowd total.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative 'decenas' cannot establish a threshold of 50; no invented lower or upper bound is used.

state_response.summary: Neither report describes an event-specific state response in a coded dimension; values remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: Neither report establishes whether protesters used violence; silence is not coded as no.

state_target.summary: Participants marched to the Supreme Court and demanded justice and stricter laws; code remains provisional for coordinator review.

notes: Distinct from the same-day Pavas eviction protest by site, organizers, and demand. The 9:00 a.m. time in CR Hoy is from a quoted call, so the event's actual start time is taken from La Teja. The route endpoint is supported, but an exact end time is not.
open_questions: Verify whether simultaneous physical attendance reached 50; both sources are qualitative only.
Check event-specific reporting for coded state responses; do not infer absence from silence.
Keep the event end time unknown.

title: Competing groups gather at the Legislative Assembly during the Defensoría selection debate
location: Outside and inside the Legislative Assembly, San José
organizer: FEUNA and FEUCR called the student group opposing Erick Ulate; organizers of the pro-Ulate group are not named
participants_original: UCR's photo-gallery captions identify student and human-rights groups opposing Erick Ulate/supporting Laura Arguedas and Ulate supporters at the same site; no total is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved. The gallery confirms groups were physically present, but supplies no simultaneous crowd count or evidence of at least 50.

start_date.summary: The UCR gallery dates the resumed debate and demonstrations to Monday, Jan. 23; OPNA reports the federations' position on Jan. 23 and 24.

location.summary: The gallery captions place student/citizen groups at and inside the Legislative Assembly.

organizer.summary: The gallery attributes the student call to FEUNA and FEUCR and identifies other groups; pro-Ulate supporters' organizers are not specified.

demands.summary: Student groups opposed Erick Ulate and supported Laura Arguedas; other participants supported Ulate. The shared state process under debate was selection of the Defensoría head; group-specific demands are noted rather than treated as unanimous.

participants_original.summary: Gallery captions identify several groups but no attendee count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither the gallery nor OPNA report gives a total or proves at least 50 people were present simultaneously.

end_date.summary: No physical end date/time is reported; the legislature's debate continuing through Jan. 24 is not a protest endpoint.

state_response.summary: Sources do not establish an event-specific response in a coded dimension.

state_target.summary: The groups positioned themselves around the Legislative Assembly's choice of a national Defensoría head; this is coded provisionally as a political process demand.

notes: This is one provisional same-site/day assembly record, not an assumption that opposing groups had a shared demand or organizer.
